fatal_errors: The hypothesis substitutes a coarse-grained Cantor-type alloy in chloride solution for the specified lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA tested against identically conditioned DS2205 in deionized water.
It misses the target governing variable: temperature-dependent competition among depassivation, repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and oxidative or third-body wear.
It incorrectly associates the inverse Hall–Petch effect with enhanced hardness; inverse Hall–Petch behavior denotes softening at extremely small grain sizes.
The proposed static-corrosion baseline has no wear rate, so the predicted reduction in wear rate relative to that baseline is not scientifically defined.

Vacuum-versus-NaCl testing changes both environmental chemistry and lubrication/contact mechanics and therefore cannot by itself attribute changes specifically to passive-film degradation by grain boundaries.

The cited evidence does not establish that sliding creates the proposed nanocrystalline or amorphous layer, that this layer controls tribo-corrosion, or that it simultaneously lowers wear and accelerates corrosion.
explanation: The response addresses tribo-corrosion in a broad sense and supplies a testable alternative involving a deformation-induced surface layer, but it does not reconstruct the target material, comparator, thermal-shock treatment, deionized-water conditions, temperature/load/frequency matrix, or observed nonmonotonic temperature response. It consequently misses the central result: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 retained its L12/B2 lamellar structure and outperformed DS2205, with minimum degradation near 50 °C because repassivation and a stable low-shear tribo-layer were favored there, while abrasion dominated at 25 °C and film disruption or debris-assisted wear dominated at 100 °C. The proposed controls and electrochemical measurements could test part of the alternative idea, but they do not cleanly partition mechanical wear, corrosion, and synergy. Evidence E1 only links processing-derived fine grains and residual stress to weaker passivity, while E2 concerns UHV friction and ultrananocrystalline mechanics; neither directly supports the asserted tribo-induced layer or its claimed coupled effect. The internal misuse of inverse Hall–Petch behavior further weakens mechanistic validity.
